thread:
alex: Heads up — multiple customers and a canary hit weird timeouts after the latest publish. Symptoms look like connection churn + mis-typed config values.
sophie: I saw that too. p95 for short prompts shot up and socket resets ticked. Any recent pool/typing changes?
ben: There were three related changes: 1) a typed PoolConfig dataclass landed in #517, 2) env loader refactor in #521 that attempted to coerce envs to annotated types, and 3) the streaming iterator refactor in #525. The combination may be exposing a few edge cases.
alex: Example log: 
```
2026-03-27T09:11:02Z ERROR req=kk21 pool_wait=302ms inflight=88 max_connections=128 error=TimeoutError: request timed out after 5s
2026-03-27T09:11:02Z WARN config: SESSION_LIFETIME=\"90\" parsed_as=90 (string provided)
2026-03-27T09:11:02Z WARN stream: abandoned iterator detected, stream_abandoned_count=3
```
harry: Two separate customers had SESSION_LIFETIME set via Helm as a quoted value. Our env coercer accepted the string but later code paths expected an int and used it to compute expiration windows incorrectly, shortening sessions. That caused TLS reconnect churn.
sophie: Repro steps I used: run `bench_small.py` with many short concurrent requests and occasionally cancel streaming iterators early. On the patched branch I see fd increase when cancellations happen and early GC doesn't close background readers from stream refactor.
ben: Actions proposed: 
- immediate: publish a patch that makes env coercion stricter (warn on quoted numerics) and roll that to canary, and add a startup metric `sdk.config.parse_warnings`.
- fix streaming: add a finalizer + explicit aclose in stream iterator and unit test for early cancellation.
- pool defaults: increase default semaphore from 16 -> 64 until we have a better adaptive algorithm; add docs about recommended values for high QPS short calls.
- tests: add integration smoke that runs 5k short requests with random cancels to catch both starvation and leaks.
sophie: For DX: update quickstart/k8s examples to show unquoted numerics and mention common env gotchas in the onboarding FAQ. Also export PoolConfig with types so IDEs catch errors.
harry: I'll open PRs: #533 (env coercion strict + metric), #534 (stream finalizer + tests), #535 (docs/quickstart updates). I'll also add a temporary runtime flag `RW_POOL_SEMAPHORE_OVERRIDE` we can flip from infra while we develop adaptive heuristics.
alex: Support notes: tell affected customers to set RW_POOL_SEMAPHORE=256 and ensure SESSION_LIFETIME is unquoted for now. Support template updated.
support-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-python-sdk/issues/533 with logs and repro.
ben: Long term: adaptive session lifetime (extend when short-request ratio high), smarter fairness scheduler that avoids queue-thrashing on many short requests, and better typed public API so container manifests are less error-prone.
sophie: I'll add a short devex sample app that shows recommended PoolConfig for chat vs. embedding workloads and an `examples/quickstart/helm-values.yaml` change.
alex: Thanks team. Can we ship the env coercion patch to canary this afternoon? Risk is low and it should reduce silent misconfigs.
harry: Will do.
